caption: The video captures a static overhead view of a flat sandy surface holding several motionless objects. A white plastic basin rests in a dark wet-sand patch on the left, while a short brown cylinder lies diagonally near the center beside an upright red-and-black marker. On the right, a second dark wet-sand patch cradles a tangled pile of brightly colored thin sticks together with a green spoon-shaped item. A thin vertical pole shadow and a small device shadow fall across the lower-center of the frame. The whole scene is brightly lit, so these shadows read clearly against the pale sand, and every object holds its exact position and orientation without any visible translation, rotation, or occlusion. The visible change is then a temporary dip in illumination. The scene darkens noticeably and the lower pole and device shadows fade out, while the basin, cylinder, marker, and stick pile remain fixed in place. After this dim interval the lighting returns to the brighter state, the shadows reappear, and the layout stays unchanged through the final frame.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
